newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian shares end firmer, seen heading higher.
newsitem.headline: Austrian shares end firmer, seen heading higher.

text.p: Austrian shares ended on a robust note on Tuesday, buoyed by selective buying interest on slim turnover, and traders said the next target for the ATX blue chip index would be 1,080 points.
The ATX index of 21 shares climbed 5.85 points, or 0.55 percent, to 1,076. Among its constituents 14 stocks rose, five fell and two remained unchanged.
"The trend is friendly," said one trader. "Particularly with...the current bond strength, the index should push further upwards."
The results of U.S. elections were not expected to have a major impact on the market.
"I don't see what surprises the polls could bring," said one trader. The key question was whether the Republicans would keep their majority in the U.S. congress, he noted.

Engineering group VA Technologie was among the day's best performers. Its shares ended at 1,539.6 schillings, off an all-time high of 1,548 touched earlier in the session. Traders said the gains were technically led.
The leading gainer was index heavyweight insurer EA Generali, jumping 90 schillings or 2.81 percent, to 3,290.
Papermaker Leykam was the leading decliner, shedding one schilling to 296.
The broad-based Vienna Bourse index added 2.75 points or 0.67 percent to 413.22
The November ATX future rose 8.9 points to 1,077.5 on volume of 360 contracts.
